figure1_genetic_code.png: The genetic code confines 8-oxoguanine transcriptional miscoding to 18 amino-acid substitutions. (a) Base pairing at the polymerase active site, where template guanine pairs with cytosine through Watson-Crick geometry while 8-oxoguanine can rotate to the syn conformation and pair with adenine through Hoogsteen-like geometry, giving a coding-sense C>A change in the transcript, with hydrogen bonds dashed and geometry following published RNA polymerase II elongation-complex structures [6]. (b) All ordered amino-acid pairs, with purple marking the 18 pairs reachable by a coding-sense C>A change, gray the 132 reachable by another single-base change and pale gray the 230 requiring more than one. (c) Residues this route can replace and can introduce, where outlined codes mark the eight residues accessible in one direction only.
figure2_disease_convergence.png: Accessible substitutions intersect 3,910 disease-associated protein states, including 211 that can arise while the disease-associated nucleotide remains wild type. (a) States per substitution class, with open blue circles for all accessible states and filled blue circles for the higher-confidence subset. (b) GJB1 phenylalanine 51 as a worked example, where rust marks the nucleotide altered by the pathogenic genomic allele and purple the nucleotide altered by the C>A transcriptional route, both producing leucine. (c) States by the relationship between the genomic and transcriptional routes within the codon, with purple marking the different-position class and values given as totals with the higher-confidence subset in parentheses. (d) The two codon configurations that account for all different-position states, with rust and purple as in panel b.
figure3_gene_context.png: Chemically accessible disease-associated states vary with combined post-mitotic expression and neurological disease annotation. (a) Accessible fractions across eight Human Protein Atlas single-cell expression classes, with blue points showing observed values, gray bars the 95% gene-label permutation intervals and gray ticks the permutation means, where neurons were the only class surviving correction (†q = 0.004). (b) Accessible fractions jointly stratified by post-mitotic expression and neurological disease annotation, with whole-gene bootstrap intervals and the interaction estimate of the joint gene-level model shown on the panel. (c) Pathway associations with 95% confidence intervals on a logarithmic odds-ratio axis, colored by family, where every displayed pathway passed a q value below 0.05 and was selected by the prespecified rule described in Methods.
figure4_proteomic_observation.png: C>A-accessible protein states are observed in human tissues among substitutions unexplained by sample-specific transcript sequence. (a) Stepped filtering cascade from confidently localized substitution sites to the states reachable at the exact codon position, with the count printed inside each step, uniform step widths that do not encode those counts and the accent color marking only the final group. (b) The 78 accessible states by substitution class. (c) The 12 genes with the most observed accessible states, ranked by count and then alphabetically, with hemoglobin genes highlighted.
figureS1_specification_sensitivity.png: Specification sensitivity of the gene-context interaction. Points are odds ratios for the interaction between post-mitotic expression and neurological disease annotation and horizontal bars are 95% intervals, with the primary specification in rust. The whole-gene bootstrap row uses percentile intervals and all others use heteroskedasticity-robust Wald intervals. The final row restricts accessible states to the 2,146 coordinates detected in published oxidized-guanine maps, which is a sensitivity analysis rather than a redefinition of the primary catalog, and the vertical line marks an odds ratio of 1.
figureS2_lesion_evidence.png: Oxidized-guanine map evidence at accessible coordinates. (a) Proportion of coordinates detected in at least one published oxidized-guanine map, comparing the accessible disease-associated coordinates with route-matched missense-capable coding cytosines in the same transcripts, with counts printed above each point, the odds ratio and its 95% confidence interval from a two-sided Fisher exact test shown on the panel. (b) The 78 observed accessible states partitioned into the four mutually exclusive lesion-support categories, with the single unresolved state labeled above its segment.
